response.sql:
WITH proj_ratio AS (
  SELECT p.arcregistry AS project_id,
         p.fundflux AS funding_source,
         SUM(s.boxx) / NULLIF(SUM(s.boxz), 0) AS ratio
  FROM scanspatial s
  JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref
  GROUP BY p.arcregistry, p.fundflux
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT project_id,
         funding_source,
         ratio,
         ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY funding_source) AS excess
  FROM proj_ratio
)
SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, excess
FROM ranked
ORDER BY excess DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Each project has one funding source (projects.arcregistry is the primary key), so grouping by project and fundflux gives one row per project. Spatial rows with no matching project are dropped by the inner join.
SUM ignores NULL boxx and boxz values separately, as the request specifies. A project whose boxz total is zero or missing gets a NULL ratio (via NULLIF), and that NULL ratio sorts last.
Projects with a NULL fundflux form their own funding-source group. The PARTITION BY treats NULLs as one group, so their average is taken over those projects.
The ratio averages over a funding source skip projects whose ratio is NULL (AVG ignores NULLs). Ties in excess have no defined order.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude projects with no funding source (NULL fundflux) entirely, so they are neither ranked nor used in any average.
alternatives.sql:
WITH proj_ratio AS (
  SELECT p.arcregistry AS project_id,
         p.fundflux AS funding_source,
         SUM(s.boxx) / NULLIF(SUM(s.boxz), 0) AS ratio
  FROM scanspatial s
  JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref
  WHERE p.fundflux IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY p.arcregistry, p.fundflux
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT project_id,
         funding_source,
         ratio,
         ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY funding_source) AS excess
  FROM proj_ratio
)
SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, excess
FROM ranked
ORDER BY excess DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
